ledger.note: 3 September 301: San Marino claims its founding. The country 'claims to have been founded in AD 301'; the date is traditional, the first historical evidence is a monastic community of the 5th or 6th century, and the feast of 3 September commemorates the origin. [fx-43 R035] San Marino page: the country is 'officially the Republic of San Marino', independence '3 September 301 (traditional)'. The dossier republic-of-san-marino (founded 301, same cell, Cliopatria shapes 1797 and 1799) describes the same state; this dossier keeps the ledger and now carries the Cliopatria name 'Republic of San Marino', Wikidata Q238 and the reviews of the two shapes. The other dossier is for the orchestrator to retire (handoff).
1320: Chiesanuova joins San Marino. 'The community of Chiesanuova chose to join the country' (the page: '1320 (earlier extension)'). The page names no previous holder.

1463: San Marino acquires four castles. 'Faetano, Fiorentino, Montegiardino, and Serravalle were added to the country. Since then, the country's borders have remained unchanged.' The History of San Marino page (second page): 'the republic entered into an alliance against Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta, duke of Rimini, who was later defeated'; 'As a result, Pope Pius II gave San Marino some castles and the towns of Fiorentino, Montegiardino and Serravalle'; 'Later that year, the town of Faetano joined the republic on its own accord.' Neither page says who held the castles before, so the counterpart stays nobody; the Malatesta of Rimini, the enemy of that war, are the likely holders but no page says so.

1503: Cesare Borgia occupies San Marino. In 1503 Borgia, the son of Pope Alexander VI, 'occupied the Republic for six months until his father's successor, Pope Julius II, intervened and restored the country's independence' (San Marino page; the History of San Marino page: 'In 1503, Cesare Borgia occupied the Republic until the death of his father some months later'). Neither page gives a month. The counterpart is a reading: the occupier is Borgia, whose Duchy of Romagna the papal-states dossier carries as a vassal from 1500 to 1503, and it is the pope who ends the occupation.

1503: Pope Julius II restores San Marino's independence. 'Pope Julius II intervened and restored the country's independence' after six months (San Marino page). Neither page dates the end, and a six-month occupation that began in 1503 could end in 1504, so the year is a bridge over the pages' silence.

17 October 1739: the papal legate of Ravenna occupies San Marino. 'The country was occupied on 17 October 1739 by the legate (Papal governor) of Ravenna, Cardinal Giulio Alberoni'; the History of San Marino page adds that he 'used military force'.

5 February 1740: Pope Clement XII restores San Marino's independence. 'Independence was restored by Pope Clement XII on 5 February 1740' (San Marino page); the History of San Marino page: 'On 5 February 1740, three and a half months after the occupation began, the Pope recognised San Marino's rights, restoring independence.'

September 1944: German forces briefly occupy San Marino. 'In September 1944, it was briefly occupied by German forces,' who were defeated by the Allies in the Battle of San Marino; Allied bombers had struck on 26 June 1944. The Battle of San Marino page (second page) dates it: 'On 13 September, the German Army sent a strong force into San Marino to defend it against the Allies'.

September 1944: the Germans are driven out in the Battle of San Marino. The San Marino page gives no day; the Battle of San Marino page (second page) dates the battle 17-20 September 1944 and says 'The city was captured by the afternoon of 20 September'.

20 September 1944: Allied troops take San Marino. 'The city was captured by the afternoon of 20 September' and 'Allied forces remained in occupation of San Marino for a short period after the German surrender' (Battle of San Marino page); the San Marino page: 'Allied troops then occupied the country for two months before departing.' The page's infobox lists the United Kingdom and British India as the Allied belligerents (the 4th Indian Infantry Division, with a 'thrust up the eastern seaboard by the British Eighth Army'), so the counterpart is the United Kingdom; british-raj is named in the war's belligerents. 'A military government was not set up due to Sammarinese neutrality'.

About November 1944: the Allied troops leave. The San Marino page gives 'two months' after the September battle and no month (the History of San Marino page repeats 'stayed only for two months before leaving'), so November is arithmetic. The Battle of San Marino page says 'the 4th Indian Division left the country on the 21st' (September) while 'Allied forces remained in occupation ... for a short period after the German surrender' with no date; the pages do not agree and none dates the departure of the last troops.

wars.name: Battle of San Marino
wars.outcome: German forces entered the neutral Republic on 13 September 1944 and were attacked by Allied forces (the 4th Indian Infantry Division with the British Eighth Army, 17-20 September); the city was captured by the afternoon of 20 September. The Allies occupied the country for a short period (two months on the San Marino page) and set up no military government; borders unchanged.
wars.note: Battle of San Marino page: infobox dates 17-20 September 1944, German side the 278th Infantry Division, Allied side the 4th Indian Infantry Division, belligerent states the United Kingdom and British India (the first version's placeholder 'Allied forces' is replaced by united-kingdom and british-raj). San Marino itself was neutral: it is listed as the ground, not a side.

certainty.note: Founding and early extent are traditional; the page's earliest evidence is a monastic community of the 5th or 6th century.

sources.title: History of San Marino
sources.note: Third page, beyond the two-page budget, opened for the review: 1463 gifts of Pius II and Faetano, Malatesta of Rimini named only as the enemy, Borgia 1503 'some months', Alberoni 1739 and 5 February 1740, Allies 'two months'.

notes: A micro-state Cliopatria lacks. Pages opened: San Marino, then (for the review fixes) Battle of San Marino and History of San Marino, one over the two-page budget. The Congress of Vienna is not on the pages. Papal protection from 1631 'never amounted to a de facto Papal control' (page), so no vassal event; the 1862 Convention of Friendship with the Kingdom of Italy is a treaty, not a border event; Napoleon's 1797 offer to extend the territory was declined by the regents. Occupations on the ledger: Cesare Borgia 1503 (counterpart papal-states, a reading), the papal legate of Ravenna 17 October 1739 to 5 February 1740, the Germans from 13 September 1944, the Allies (united-kingdom) from 20 September 1944 for about two months. The previous holder of the 1320 and 1463 additions is on no page opened (counterpart nobody). No ruler strip: the Captains Regent change every six months (1 April and 1 October). The end year 2026 is the project's last year.
